VISIT_CONTEXT.treatment_goal: Control platinum-resistant relapse while balancing efficacy, toxicity, surgery preference, trial access, and quality of life.

patient_preferences.notes: Patient wants high response probability and strongly prefers another surgery if complete resection is realistically feasible. She is willing to discuss clinical trials if this does not meaningfully delay treatment. She wants to avoid meaningful vision loss but would complete baseline ophthalmology and feasible monitoring if expected benefit is compelling; ophthalmology follow-up is 3-4 hours away and outpatient care is preferred.

PLATINUM_HISTORY.evidence: First recurrence occurred more than 12 months after first-line platinum completion.
Second recurrence occurred after a long platinum-free interval following carboplatin/gemcitabine/bevacizumab.
Progression occurred 103 days after third-line carboplatin-containing therapy.

SURGERY_DONE.procedure: Interval cytoreductive surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, and peritoneal tumor debulking; no gross residual disease documented.

ADJUVANT_TREATMENT.cycles_or_courses: Three postoperative cycles after three neoadjuvant cycles

LINE_OF_THERAPY.regimen: Carboplatin plus paclitaxel followed by interval cytoreductive surgery, then carboplatin plus paclitaxel plus bevacizumab

discontinuation.detail: Completed planned first-line therapy and transitioned to maintenance.

CASE_CORE.CURRENT_STATUS: Platinum-resistant recurrent high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma with abdomen/pelvis-confined measurable disease, rapid CA125/HE4 rise, ECOG 1, prior bevacizumab and PARP inhibitor exposure. Current recurrence biopsy shows heterogeneous FRalpha expression, PD-L1 CPS 18, HER2 2+/rare focal 3+ with ISH non-amplified, CCNE1 amplification, HRD negative, and no pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. Patient strongly prefers surgery if complete resection is realistic. Imaging shows no definite distant FDG-avid disease, with sigmoid/small-bowel mesenteric nodularity, bowel-serosal contact, small ascites, and prior cytoreductions. Hypertension/proteinuria after bevacizumab and baseline ocular disease are documented concurrent issues.
